name: Chevron

summary.text: Chevron Corporation is a U.S. oil major that acquired Texaco in 2001. In February 2011 an Ecuadorian court in Lago Agrio ordered Chevron to pay roughly $9 billion (later put at $9.5 billion after reduction by Ecuador's highest court) for oil contamination attributed to Texaco's former operations in the Amazon. Chevron sued the plaintiffs' U.S. lawyer Steven Donziger under RICO in New York; U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan found in 2014 that the Ecuadorian judgment was procured by fraud and bribery and barred its enforcement in the United States, and the Second Circuit affirmed in August 2016. Donziger was later convicted of criminal contempt for defying court orders in that litigation and served a six-month sentence; the Second Circuit affirmed in 2022 and the Supreme Court declined review in 2023. On this site Chevron also appears among the oil majors sued by U.S. states and cities over climate deception.

facts.claim: On February 14, 2011 an Ecuadorian court ordered Chevron to pay about $9 billion in damages for oil contamination in the Amazon attributed to Texaco, which Chevron acquired in 2001; Chevron reported that the award would roughly double if it did not issue a public apology, and Ecuador's highest court later upheld the judgment at a reduced $9.5 billion.

facts.claim: In Chevron's RICO suit against Steven Donziger, U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan found that Donziger and his team had paid court-appointed experts who posed as neutral, submitted fraudulent evidence and ghost-wrote the Ecuadorian judgment, and he enjoined enforcement of the judgment in U.S. courts and imposed a constructive trust over any proceeds.

facts.claim: On August 8, 2016 a Second Circuit panel unanimously affirmed the RICO judgment, finding no basis for dismissal or reversal, describing the defendants' conduct as including fabricating evidence and bribing the Ecuadorian judge, and remanding for determination of the fees Donziger owed Chevron; the Supreme Court later denied certiorari.

facts.claim: On September 7, 2018 an arbitral tribunal found that Ecuador had violated its bilateral investment treaty with the United States by allowing its courts to issue the Lago Agrio judgment.

sources.title: Panel Protects Chevron in Ecuador Case

facts.claim: After Donziger refused a 2019 order to surrender his electronic devices, Judge Kaplan charged him with criminal contempt; federal prosecutors declined the case and the court appointed private lawyers from Seward & Kissel as special prosecutors. On July 26, 2021 Judge Loretta Preska found Donziger guilty on all six counts, and in October 2021 he was sentenced to six months in prison.

facts.claim: On June 22, 2022 the Second Circuit affirmed Donziger's contempt conviction, holding that the district court did not plainly err in appointing special prosecutors under Supreme Court precedent (Young v. United States ex rel. Vuitton et Fils); Judge Menashi dissented. On March 27, 2023 the Supreme Court denied certiorari, with Justice Gorsuch, joined by Justice Kavanaugh, dissenting from the denial.

facts.claim: On January 13, 2025 the U.S. Supreme Court denied two petitions by fossil-fuel companies seeking review of the Hawaii Supreme Court's decision allowing Honolulu's climate-deception claims to proceed; the Solicitor General had urged denial and Justice Alito did not participate.
